name: Calder & Rhys Wool Trenchcoat
description:
A double-breasted wool trench in the classic tradition — belted, storm-flapped, with deep slash pockets and a half-lining in printed silk-analog. Calder & Rhys is a Tier 3 to 4 label that has been making this exact coat in various colorways for forty years. The wool is a medium-weight boiled blend from their New Glasgow mill, substantial enough to cut wind without being stiff. Current season runs in charcoal, toffee, and a deep burgundy that photographs like blood in low light. The collar sits high and wide, and the lapels are cut in a slightly exaggerated proportion that reads as deliberate rather than oversized.

This is the coat you buy when you want to look like you have your life together. Architects wear it. Mid-level corporate analysts wear it. Journalists who cover the Spire but live in Tier 3 wear it. It has no tech features, no embedded sensors — it is simply a very good wool trench made by people who have been making very good wool trenches for a long time. The belt almost always goes untied, draped rather than cinched. It reads as polished and understated, which is exactly the point.
what_it_says: You have taste, you have some money, and you want neither to be immediately obvious.
story_hooks: The burgundy colorway was briefly discontinued after a high-profile Tier 4 executive was photographed wearing one at the scene of a corporate espionage incident — demand quietly doubled
A character inherits one of these from a parent; inside the lining, tucked behind the half-lining stitching, is a folded document that was never meant to be found

Calder & Rhys is rumored to be getting acquired by a Vanthorpe subsidiary, which would end the New Glasgow mill operation — the last independent run of this coat is already being bought up by collectors
